https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-n.text: Ukraine recently carried out a strike on ships in the Caspian Sea, claiming that the vessels were “used in military cargo shipments involving Iran.” In addition, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed that Russia was providing “new assistance to the Iranian regime.” He said, “Since the beginning of July, we have recorded active Russian satellite surveillance of the Gulf states and US military facilities located there.”The Ukrainian accusations are important because they reveal more of the connections between Moscow and Tehran. Many of these connections were already known.Russia and Iran, along with China, are key players in seeking to change the world order and weaken the US hegemony that began in the 1990s.It's worth recalling some of the context here. Iran was a US partner during the era of the shah before the 1979 Iranian Revolution. However, the revolution did not lead Tehran to rush into the arms of Russia during the Cold War. The leaders of the revolution wanted to pursue a third way between the US and the Soviets.They also had to deal with the fact that the Soviets were in Afghanistan at the time, and there was an Islamic insurgency there against the Russians. The Iran-Iraq war also began in the 1980s, and the Soviets supplied Iraq with arms.Iran begins developing missile programIn the 1990s, things began to change.The Soviet Union collapsed, and the Russians left Afghanistan. America's hegemony and what former president George H.W Bush called the “New World Order” had begun. Russia and Iran were now relatively weak powers in that new world order.Beginning around 1992, just after the Gulf War, Russia has played an important role in supporting Iran's missile and nuclear capabilities over several decades. Moscow helped complete Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant and has continued nuclear cooperation through the Russian state nuclear company Rosatom.This matters because the United States had shown what its new military power looked like with the Revolution in Military Affairs (RMA) – a shift toward asymmetric, low-cost, high-impact capabilities. Precision weapons and technology had destroyed the Iraqi army. Iran and Russia had to bide their time.Times were changing. In 1996, China founded the SCO, which included Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan. The economic bloc known as BRICS also began to take shape in the late 1990s and early 2000s. For Iran, this produced an opportunity to work with non-Western countries, including Russia and China. This relationship has provided Tehran with access to Russian expertise and technology.Iran was developing its missile program: Technology appears to have come from North Korea, China, and various other sources. Russian entities were accused of transferring missile-related technology to Iran. The result was a relationship in which Russia has helped Iran preserve important strategic capabilities. For Moscow, this made sense. Iran could help balance the US. It was a long road back for Moscow to confront the West.Russia's Vladimir Putin was willing to bide his time. This concept was also adopted by China. China's approach, what it called “hide your strength, bide your time,” often associated with the phrase “tao guang yang hui,” emerged under Deng Xiaoping as China rebuilt its economy and international position after the Mao era.Deng emphasized avoiding confrontation while accumulating economic and national power. China's leader Jiang Zemin largely maintained this cautious approach during the 1990s, as did Hu Jintao after 2002, despite China's rapidly expanding economic power and increasing influence.Under Xi Jinping, who came to power in 2012, China has increasingly departed from this restraint.Beijing's military strength is expanding, and it has adopted what is sometimes called “wolf warrior diplomacy,” China's more assertive and sometimes confrontational diplomatic style, particularly associated with the Xi Jinping era.Chinese diplomats increasingly challenge criticism of Beijing publicly, including on social media, and aggressively defend China's policies.Putin felt Moscow had been humiliated in the 1990s, especially during the Kosovo war. He rebuilt Russian power slowly, first defeating the Chechens and then fighting Georgia in 2008.In 2014, Russia invaded Crimea and eastern Ukraine's Donbas.In 2015, Moscow intervened in Syria. Russia and Iran worked together in Syria. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force head Qasem Soleimani is credited with having encouraged Putin to intervene.For years, the Russians and Iranians dominated at the Astana talks – sponsored by Russia, Turkey, and Iran, and hosted by Kazakhstan.However, things began to change after the invasion of Ukraine. Designed to accelerate the decline of the West and reshape world order, the invasion has not gone as planned for Moscow. Iran helped Moscow by supplying it with Shahed drones. Used in the thousands to terrorize Ukrainians, the Iranian drones have not helped Russia win the war.Russia-Iran connection key to 2015 nuclear dealAs such, the Iran-Russia connection has not actually enabled either country to achieve major wins.However, each country sees it as in its interest to help the other confront the US and the West. There is also an interplay here. Moscow was involved in supporting Iran's 2015 nuclear deal.The Russia-Iran connection was key to the deal. When former president Barack Obama entered office in 2009, his administration sought a “reset” with Russia while making Iran's nuclear program a major diplomatic priority.One early decision was to abandon the Bush administration's planned missile-defense deployments in Poland and the Czech Republic, replacing them with a different, phased missile-defense architecture.The administration argued the change better addressed the evolving Iranian missile threat, while Moscow welcomed the decision. Obama subsequently sought Russian cooperation in talking with Tehran. Russia participated in the P5+1 negotiations that eventually produced the 2015 nuclear agreement. Moscow was able to be both a strategic competitor and pretend to be a “good cop” diplomatic partner for Washington.This is the broader context of how we got here. Russia has backed Iran for many years. It wants a multi-polar world order. Other countries, such as Pakistan and Turkey, also want this multi-polar world. It's plausible that Russia sees the US and Israeli conflict with Iran as an opportunity.Moscow assumes the world will be distracted by the war and that it will use US resources, including munitions, which will mean fewer munitions for Ukraine.Iran sees the conflict as one that spans thousands of kilometers of frontlines in the Middle East, from Jordan to Lebanon, Iraq, and Yemen.Russia likely sees it as a world struggle. China does as well. What this means is that Moscow would like to use Iran against the US in the same way Russia believes Ukraine was used against Moscow.

https://www.dw.com/en/indonesia-flights-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Lgk3 The eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau saw lava sprouting and spewing of ash that was detected even 150 kilometers away Image: PVMBG/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Hundreds of flights were canceled at Jakarta's international airport after Indonesia 's Anak Krakatau volcano erupted early Sunday morning, more than 150 kilometers (93 miles) away. The volcano produced a fountain of lava and loud sounds heard up to 700 kilometers away, Indonesia's geological agency said in a statement. The cloud of ash was detected up to a height of 6,000 meters (20,000 feet) on the Java side of the volcano and a plume of up to 15,000 meters on the ‌Sumatra side and some parts of Banten province in Java, the ‌meteorological ​agency BMKG posted on its website. No incidents of casualties were reported, and no evacuation orders were issued. Danger remains in Indonesia in the wake of volcano eruptions To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The closest township is more than 16 kilometers away, but the authorities warned residents and visitors to stay at least 3 kilometers from the volcano 's active crater. Two new eruptions were recorded on Sunday, the volcanology agency warned. Indonesia cancels flights The ash spread across parts of the capital Jakarta and Lampung province on the southern tip of Sumatra island, Indonesia's Center for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation said. Authorities have suspended operations at six airports following eruptions from Mount Anak Krakatoa, the ministry said. "The Husein Sastranegara Airport in Bandung showed indications of being affected. Consequently, we have declared... the airport closed to flights," Dudy Purwagandhi told a press conference Sunday, mentioning the latest airport to be shuttered. Operations at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport, the country's largest and in the capital, Jakarta, were suspended earlier. Soekarno-Hatta International Airport posted on ‌Instagram that it had ⁠suspended ⁠flight operations until 9:30 a.m. (0230 GMT) due to volcanic ash. New volcano eruptions hit Indonesia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video "Due to increased activity from the Mount Anak Krakatau eruption, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport has temporarily suspended flight operations from 5:30 a.m. to 9.30 a.m.," the airport said. The disruption of flight operations has impacted more than 22,000 passengers, the transport ministry said in a statement, adding that 209 flights were affected, particularly to and from Singapore. Anak Krakatau lies in the middle between Java and Sumatra in Indonesia's vast island chain, which sits on the Pacific "Ring of Fire," where earthquakes and volcanic eruptions are frequent. Anak Krakatau means "Child of Krakatau." The volcano is the offspring of the famous Krakatau , whose monumental eruption in 1883 triggered a period of global cooling. https://www.kcra.com/article/roseville-r.text: The Romanian Festival is taking over Vernon Street Town Square in downtown Roseville Saturday, offering a lively cultural celebration. It is the largest Romanian cultural event on the West Coast and will feature live music, traditional Romanian dancing and authentic Romanian food. Event organizer Boris Budac joined KCRA 3 Saturday morning to discuss the festivities. "It's the largest event on the West Coast, and it is very unique. It is something that we've built over 25 years," Budac said. "It's just a beautiful day of culture to share with the broader Sacramento region." The festival is from noon until 9 p.m. on Saturday. It is open to all ages and admission and parking are free. https://www.dw.com/en/spain-train-crash-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OnZ7 Prefer DW on Google A high speed train slammed into the back of a stationary train Image: Javier Soriano/AFP Advertisement Spain began three days of national mourning on Thursday in remembrance of the 68 people killed in one of Europe's deadliest train disasters in recent memory. On Wednesday morning, a high-speed train run by state operator RENFE slammed into the back of a stationary train operated by private Italian-Spanish company Iryo in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha, south of Madrid. A British tourist who was rescued from the RENFE train told the Associated Press that "suddenly, everything started falling apart." "We realized carriage two, carriage one, all gone, all smashed. There was blood all over," the man said. Josimar Medina, a 31-year-old Peruvian who was on holiday in Spain with his girlfriend, said he was sleeping on the RENFE train when "I woke up and I was in the air." Pablo Mejia, 42, escaped with injuries to his head, telling the AFP news agency that a last-minute change of seat saved his life. He recounted "a very strong hit ... a lot of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos," while wearing a bloodstained jumper and holding a tattered suitcase. "I think I've been born again," he said. Workers started to use cranes to move parts of the damaged trains late on Wednesday Image: Oscar Del Pozo/AFP Emergency crews work through the night Emergency crews continued searching through the wreckage overnight for survivors and bodies, using cranes to move mangled metal. Relatives of passengers gathered at nearby facilities seeking information about missing loved ones. Residents of the nearby town of Urda joined emergency workers in helping survivors, providing first aid supplies, water and blankets. Protesters gather outside the Ministry of Transportation to demand accountability Image: Ananda Manjón/Europa Press/IMAGO Teams of Red Cross workers offered support. Red Cross psychologist Carmen Garcia told AFP news agency that many people are in shock and "haven't taken on board what has happened." "The grieving will be complicated," Garcia said. Crash survivors wait to board buses outside a municipal center Image: Susana Vera/REUTERS Authorities are collecting DNA samples from relatives in Madrid , Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to help identify the missing. Spain's rail network safety in question Wednesday's crash was Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year and has raised fresh questions about rail safety. Transport Minister Oscar Puente blamed the crash on an "inexplicable" decision to allow one train to continue after an automatic control system failed along a stretch of track. He said the RENFE high-speed train had travelled about 25 kilometers before hitting the stationary Iryo train. Audio recordings reveal pre-crash exchanges On Wednesday evening, Spanish media published audio recordings revealing confused conversations between the train drivers and the railways control center in the 30 minutes before the crash. In one recording pubblished by the El Pais newspaper, among others, a control center operator appears to instruct the driver of the RENFE train to resume his journey at normal speed after some technical issues. "Continue your journey and then proceed ... at normal speed [and] with normal operation," the operator tells the driver. "At normal speed?" queries the driver, to which the controller confirms: "Yes." A few minutes later, in another recording, the driver of the Iryo train then informs the control center that she is "stationary in front of the entry signal at [the town of] Urda" — about 25 kilometers (15.5 miles) ahead of the RENFE train. When she is still told to "resume the journey" normally, she says she cannot because of the security system error, reiterating that this is why she is stationary. The second recording suggests therefore that the control center was aware of the stationary Iryo train having already instructed the RENFE train to travel towards it — but no further action appears to have been taken. Spanish PM pledges full investigation Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez , who visited the crash site, pledged a full investigation and measures to strengthen rail safety. "It is clear that we need to reinforce the safety of our train service to rebuild the trust in our high-speed rail," Sanchez said. "It is not acceptable for a country like Spain to endure two high-speed train accidents in the same year." In January, 46 people died when a high-speed train derailed and collided with another in the southern Andalusia region. The latest disaster comes just weeks before Spain's November 29 general election which Prime Minister Sanchez had called hoping to leverage a wave of discontent over housing costs and high rents — and distract from right-wing attacks on his liberal migration policies and accusations of corruption against his party and his wife, which they both deny. About an hour before Wednesday's crash spread, Sanchez had posted a campaign message on social media reading: "There are lots of reasons to be optimistic about this country." Within 24 hours, Transport Minister Puente was facing calls to resign while Sanchez's main rival, conservative Popular Party leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo, demanded a full investigation of the crash and canceled campaign events for the day. "This is the moment to respect the dead, the injured and their families," Nunez Feijoo said. "But that does not mean we will ignore the fact that Spaniards are asking tough questions that demand answers." There was noticeably less restraint on show from Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, who will be hoping to enter a coalition government with the conservatives. "More dead. Another tragedy. More rage over being left to fend for ourselves, the despair and the betrayal that Spaniards are enduring," he said, refusing to join Nunez Feijoo's campaign pause. "I promise to work tirelessly until this government, which is a criminal organization, is sitting in a courtroom to answer for its crimes," he said.
